records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 towing unit 2 [roadway] 57. unit 3 towing unit 4, unit 5 towing unit 6, and unit 7 were disabled in the roadway on the nueces river bridge facing east due to a crash. unit 8, a pedestrian, was also on the roadway after having exited unit 5 from the previous crash. the roadway was iced over and there was freezing rain. unit 1 towing unit 2 proceeded to attempt to avoid the disabled units and pedestrian by driving in the middle of both lanes of travel. unit 1 then failed to [roadway] and proceeded to strike unit 3, the pedestrian, and unit 5. unit 5 then struck unit 7's passenger side with its driver side causing unit 7 to strike the concrete barrier with its left side. units 3 and 5 then proceeded to hit the concrete barrier with its right side and left side, respectively. due to the collision, units 4 and units 6 became detached from their power units. unit 1 towing unit 2 then continued [roadway] and striking the concrete barrier with unit 1's right side. unit 1 towing unit 2 then came to rest facing west against the north concrete barrier. units 5 and 7 came to rest facing east against the north concrete barrier with unit 6 between them facing west. unit 3 and unit 4 came to rest facing east against the south concrete barrier. the driver of unit 3 was pronounced deceased on scene.

(dob: [date]), who stated that a male white, identified as, brenden andre jones (dob: [date]), intentionally and knowingly struck him with a newer model silver kia 4-door sedan with paper tags on 02/17/[roadway]. in port arthur, texas. drake stated he was outside of his house, located at [roadway]. in port arthur, when he was standing outside of a silver kia 4-door sedan, arguing with his nephew/passenger of suspect vehicle, identified as, robert joseph durman (dob: [date]). drake stated he was standing on the passenger side of the silver kia, which was facing eastbound in the roadway at [roadway]. while drake and durman were arguing, the driver of the silver kia, jones, also began arguing with drake. jones told drake, “[roadway] so i can hit you with my fucking car.” at some point during the argument, jones placed his vehicle in reverse and deliberately turned his tires towards drake and hit drake with the motor vehicle. drake stated that he was struck on his left side, went over the hood of the car, and landed on the driver side of the vehicle. drake stood up and saw that jones was placing his vehicle in reverse, and began positioning his vehicle to strike drake a second time; however, drake was able to jump out of the roadway and run into his house, where he informed the homeowner, identified as, morris daniel johnson (dob: [date]), of the auto pedestrian [medical facility] with drake, and when asked why they did not contact the police immediately, both of them stated they did not have a working telephone. johnson informed drake that he was going to bring him to the police station; however, drake stated he was in pain from being [medical facility]. i observed fresh, bloody abrasions/road rash on drake’s left arm, specifically the elbow, and his left hip. drake complained of pain to his left arm, his left wrist, elbow, left hip, and pain in his right heel. photos were taken of drake’s injuries and uploaded from my body camera. i contacted district 5 officer, officer morgan #645, and had him search the area for cameras. officer morgan stated that judice’s french market at [roadway]. has a camera pointed towards the location of the collision. [roadway]. also has two cameras, but it is unknown if they recorded the incident, as officer morgan was not able to make contact with the homeowners. [person] he does have cameras at his home, but was not able to access [roadway]. mary’s; he stated he would contact the department as soon as he was able to review the video footage. it should be noted that the familial relationship between drake and jones needs to be confirmed, if jones is and or was a family/household member. drake stated he did wish to file charges for aggravated assault w/ deadly weapon, and signed an assault form indicating so. video footage and photos of drake’s injuries have been uploaded from my body camera and unit #2482.

records.deidentified_narrative: on wednesday, february 5, 2025, at approximately 1:10 pm [roadway] [roadway], a white 2024 chevy 3500 wrecker (txlp#: t5929l) driven by julian doty (txdl#: 19444520 dob: [date]) [roadway] approaching the intersection. a white female identified as crystal germany stood in the intersection's southeast corner, [roadway] in a marked crosswalk. the right-of-way at the intersection during the crash has yet to be determined. the wrecker hit the female while she was walking in the crosswalk, and she was severely injured and taken by a life flight helicopter to [medical facility] downtown and is currently in surgery. the scene was photographed and painted with surveying paint. the female is currently in surgery at the time of this email, and her prognosis is unknown. this crash will remain open and under the investigation of the harris county vehicular crimes division. supplement: the initial investigation determined that the pedestrian, identified as unit 2, was attempting to cross from north to south on the east side of the intersection at the time of the crash. unit 1, a motor vehicle, was traveling eastbound through the intersection when it struck the pedestrian. multiple independent witnesses at the scene stated that unit 1 appeared to run a red light; however, none of the witnesses had a direct view of the eastbound signal and could not definitively confirm the signal phase facing unit 1. surveillance footage obtained from a nearby location showed that as unit 2 entered the crosswalk, the pedestrian signal was actively displaying a solid red hand with no walk symbol illuminated. this indicates that unit 2 entered the roadway against the pedestrian control device, which is a violation of texas transportation code § 552. 002(a), stating that a pedestrian may not enter a roadway when facing a steady do not walk signal. based on the timing of the signal change and the estimated position and speed of unit 1 prior to the crash, it is possible that the traffic light facing unit 1 was either yellow or red at the time of entry into the intersection, although this could not be definitively confirmed due to video limitations. should unit 1 have entered the intersection while facing a red signal, this would be a violation of texas transportation code 544. 007(d), which requires all vehicles to stop at a clearly marked stop line when facing a steady red signal. the driver of unit 1 stated he proceeded through a green light, while the pedestrian, [medical facility], advised that she had no recollection of the incident due to traumatic injuries sustained in the crash. based on the totality of the evidence, it appears that both parties may have contributed to the collision through non-compliance with [roadway] at the time of the incident. based on the evidence gathered at the scene, the review of witness statements, and the analysis of surveillance video, it is concluded that the pedestrian (unit 2) entered the crosswalk against a clearly illuminated red hand signal, failing to yield the right-of-way to vehicular traffic in accordance with texas transportation code 552. 002(a). it is further noted that while witness statements suggest the driver of unit 1 may have proceeded through a red signal, the exact signal phase at the time of entry into the intersection could not be conclusively determined due to limitations in the video evidence. therefore, while unit 1 may have potentially violated texas transportation code § 544. 007(d), that determination cannot be made with certainty. as a result, both the pedestrian and the driver of unit 1 appear to bear contributory responsibility for the crash based on failure to comply with applicable traffic control devices. no charges will be filed at this time pending any additional evidence. witness hart, ki ana, deorgiene [phone], doty, julian, edward [phone], seeberger, azalea [phone], bernard, ricky [phone].

[date]) [roadway] approaching the intersection. a white female identified as crystal germany stood in the intersection's southeast corner, [roadway] in a marked crosswalk. the right-of-way at the intersection during the crash has yet to be determined. the wrecker hit the female while she was walking in the crosswalk, and she was severely injured and taken by a life flight helicopter to [medical facility] downtown and is currently in surgery. the scene was photographed and painted with surveying paint. the female is currently in surgery at the time of this email, and her prognosis is unknown. this crash will remain open and under the investigation of the harris county vehicular crimes division. supplement: the initial investigation determined that the pedestrian, identified as unit 2, was attempting to cross from north to south on the east side of the intersection at the time of the crash. unit 1, a motor vehicle, was traveling eastbound through the intersection when it struck the pedestrian. multiple independent witnesses at the scene stated that unit 1 appeared to run a red light; however, none of the witnesses had a direct view of the eastbound signal and could not definitively confirm the signal phase facing unit 1. surveillance footage obtained from a nearby location showed that as unit 2 entered the crosswalk, the pedestrian signal was actively displaying a solid red hand with no walk symbol illuminated. this indicates that unit 2 entered the roadway against the pedestrian control device, which is a violation of texas transportation code § 552. 002(a), stating that a pedestrian may not enter a roadway when facing a steady do not walk signal. based on the timing of the signal change and the estimated position and speed of unit 1 prior to the crash, it is possible that the traffic light facing unit 1 was either yellow or red at the time of entry into the intersection, although this could not be definitively confirmed due to video limitations. should unit 1 have entered the intersection while facing a red signal, this would be a violation of texas transportation code 544. 007(d), which requires all vehicles to stop at a clearly marked stop line when facing a steady red signal. the driver of unit 1 stated he proceeded through a green light, while the pedestrian, [medical facility], advised that she had no recollection of the incident due to traumatic injuries sustained in the crash. based on the totality of the evidence, it appears that both parties may have contributed to the collision through non-compliance with [roadway] at the time of the incident. based on the evidence gathered at the scene, the review of witness statements, and the analysis of surveillance video, it is concluded that the pedestrian (unit 2) entered the crosswalk against a clearly illuminated red hand signal, failing to yield the right-of-way to vehicular traffic in accordance with texas transportation code 552. 002(a). it is further noted that while witness statements suggest the driver of unit 1 may have proceeded through a red signal, the exact signal phase at the time of entry into the intersection could not be conclusively determined due to limitations in the video evidence. therefore, while unit 1 may have potentially violated texas transportation code § 544. 007(d), that determination cannot be made with certainty. as a result, both the pedestrian and the driver of unit 1 appear to bear contributory responsibility for the crash based on failure to comply with applicable traffic control devices. no charges will be filed at this time pending any additional evidence. witness hart, ki ana, deorgiene [phone], doty, julian, edward [phone], seeberger, azalea [phone], bernard, ricky [phone].
